record.field: Odoo was originally called TinyERP when founded in 2005 by Fabien Pinckaers in Belgium.
history
The name "Odoo" was chosen in 2014 and is meant to sound friendly and approachable!
history
Odoo S.A. is headquartered in Grand-Rosière, Belgium - a small village with big software ambitions!
history
Odoo has over 12 million users worldwide and is used in 120+ countries.
history
The OWL framework (Odoo Web Library) powers all modern Odoo frontend components - including this chess game!
feature
Odoo's longpolling bus allows real-time updates without page refreshes - that's how you see your opponent's moves instantly!
feature
Odoo has 82+ official apps and over 50,000 community apps on the Odoo App Store!
feature
Odoo's QWeb templating engine renders all views - it's XML that becomes beautiful HTML!
feature
Odoo's ORM supports computed fields with dependencies - like how the current player is automatically calculated from the FEN position!
feature
Pro tip: Use Ctrl+K anywhere in Odoo to open the command palette for quick navigation!
tip
Did you know? You can click on most field labels in Odoo forms to access field-specific actions!
tip
Odoo tip: Use the "/" key in text fields to access quick formatting and block insertion options!
tip
Press "?" in most Odoo views to see available keyboard shortcuts for that view!
tip
The Odoo mascot is an elephant named "Odie" - because elephants never forget your data!
fun
Odoo Experience is the largest annual business software conference in Europe, held in Brussels!
fun
The Odoo Community Association (OCA) has contributed over 2,500 modules to the Odoo ecosystem!
fun
Odoo's purple color (#714B67) is actually called "Odoo Purple" and represents creativity and innovation!
fun
While you're playing chess, somewhere an Odoo developer is probably fixing a bug - or creating a new feature!
fun
This chess game uses python-chess for move validation - the same library used by Lichess and chess.com!
fun
The FEN notation storing your game position was invented in 1883 - older than most ERP systems!
fun
The Elo rating system used here was created by Arpad Elo in 1960 for the US Chess Federation.
fun
Before becoming Odoo, the software went through three names: TinyERP (2005), OpenERP (2009), and Odoo (2014).
history
Odoo's source code was first published on Launchpad in 2008, later moving to GitHub in 2014.
history
Fabien Pinckaers started coding TinyERP while still a student at UCLouvain in Belgium!
history
Odoo's discuss module supports real-time messaging - perfect for trash talking your chess opponent!
feature
Record rules in Odoo ensure you can only see your own chess games - security by design!
feature
Odoo's asset bundling system automatically minifies and combines JavaScript files for faster loading.
feature
The Odoo registry caches all model definitions - that's why the app runs fast after startup!
feature
Tip: Double-click on editable fields in list view to edit them inline without opening the form!
tip
Use Alt+Shift+arrow keys to navigate between records without using your mouse!
tip
Tip: Add "debug=1" to your URL to enable developer mode and see technical field names!
tip
You can export any list view to Excel by clicking the Actions menu and selecting Export!
tip
Odoo runs on PostgreSQL - one of the most reliable databases in the world!
fun
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe. Odoo can store them all!
fun
The word "checkmate" comes from the Persian phrase "shah mat" meaning "the king is helpless".
fun
The longest possible chess game is 5,949 moves. That's a lot of Odoo bus notifications!
fun
Magnus Carlsen's peak Elo rating was 2882. What's yours in Odoo Chess?
fun
The knight is the only chess piece that can jump over other pieces - and the trickiest to code!
fun
A pawn that reaches the other side can become a queen - talk about a career promotion!
fun
The fastest checkmate possible (Fool's Mate) takes only 2 moves. Don't let that be you!
